result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.k_crust()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Extract the k-crust subgraph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L21210-L21255){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.k_crust(k) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![k-crust](/assets/graphs/k-crust.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Left: the eight-node graph with a dense cluster A to D, a ring E, F, G and a pendant H. Right: the 2-crust keeps every node with coreness 2 or less, so E, F, G, H and the edges among them are in the accent color, and only the 3-core A to D is dashed." width="100%"} The k-crust contains all nodes with coreness <= `k`. This is the complement of nodes with high coreness values. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [k]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Maximum coreness value to include. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : New graph containing only the k-crust nodes and their connecting edges. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#78a5625f .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph() for i in range(5): g.add_node(label=str(i)) g.add_edge("0", "1") g.add_edge("1", "2") g.add_edge("2", "3") g.add_edge("3", "4") # Get nodes with coreness <= 2 crust_2 = g.k_crust(2) # Returns the number of nodes in the 2-crust crust_2.count_nodes() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 5 ``` ::: :::
